title: fix(i18n,app-shell): the marketplace uninstall note says the app leaves the running kernel at once (objectui#12684)
body:
Fixes #12684
Clause-②: no

## What

`marketplace.installedAdditiveNote` is the tooltip and accessible description of a loaded marketplace row's Uninstall on Setup › Packages. It told the operator that "the running kernel keeps the app registered until you restart the runtime". objectstack's `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/ID` now withdraws the package from the running kernel at once (objectstack#21576). The note is reworded in all ten packs to what was measured on a live backend:

> Uninstall removes the app from the running kernel at once, together with its permission sets and their grants, and deletes the cached manifest so the package does not load at the next start. Records stored in its objects stay in the database.

- Each pack carries its own translation, plain text, no markup (the objectui#12610 walk over the ten packs still holds).
- The comment over the render site in `MarketplaceRowActions` (above the tooltip) said the same stale thing and now follows the note. The `notLoaded` branch, which carries no note, is unchanged.
- The key name is unchanged, so the objectui#12610 tooltip and sr-only wiring and their pins are untouched.
- `ar`: the new value keeps the definite participle in `النواة الجارية` (attributive on a definite noun), so the `YA_IS_CORRECT` row of the objectui#6610 orthography pin stands as it is, with the same reason.

## Reproduction and measurement (unchanged main first)

Backend: objectstack `66d456d01` (`verify-os-12643`, used as a backend only), the showcase from a scratch copy so install-local wrote into the copy, `OS_CLOUD_URL=off`, port 4684, a persistent SQLite file. Admin `admin@objectos.ai`. Package: the compiled CRM example bundle, installed through the inline-manifest path of `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` (offline).

| Reading | After install | After DELETE, no restart | After a restart (same DB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/meta/app` names | showcase_app, setup, account, **crm_app** | showcase_app, setup, account | showcase_app, setup, account |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/permission`, the CRM sets | crm_sales_user, guest_portal | none | none |
| grant of `crm_sales_user` to the admin (`sys_user_permission_set`) | present | gone | gone |
| `GET /api/v1/data/crm_account` | 200 | 404 `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 |
| install-local ledger / cached manifest file | com.example.crm / present | empty / gone | empty / gone |
| rows in the CRM tables (SQLite, read-only) | 28 | 28 | 28 |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/object`, the CRM objects | 6 | **6** (see Acceptance notes) | 0 |

- Install answered 200, `hotLoaded: true`, 28 seed rows inserted.
- The DELETE (driven from the console's Uninstall) answered 200 with `cleanups: [{ name: "security.package-permissions", success: true, removed: 1 }]` and the server's own note "Cached manifest removed, the package withdrawn from the running kernel, and the uninstall cleanups this runtime's plugins registered ran".
- Reinstalling afterwards seeded `skipped: 28`: the rows had stayed in the database.

So the premise holds: the app leaves the running kernel at once, and a restart has nothing left to do for the app, its permission sets or its grants.

### The console, before and after

Read with Playwright from the console dev server (this worktree's source) proxied to that backend, on a loaded `com.example.crm` row at `/apps/setup/component/developer/packages?source=marketplace`.

- **Before** (main `655e897`), tooltip and sr-only description, identical: "The kernel API is additive only — uninstall removes the on-disk manifest so the package won't load on next boot, but the running kernel keeps the app registered until you restart the runtime."
- **After** (`77821a8`), en, tooltip and sr-only description, identical: the sentence quoted under What.
- **After**, zh: "卸载会立即将该应用从运行中的内核中移除，其权限集及相应授权也一并移除；同时删除缓存的清单，下次启动时不再加载该包。其对象中已存储的记录仍保留在数据库中。"

## Pins

Added to `MarketplaceRowActions.installedAppsPins.test.tsx`, beside the objectui#12610 pins, which are not edited:

- `Packages — the kernel note says the app leaves the running kernel at once (objectui#12684)` [en, zh]: a loaded row's Uninstall, read as its accessible description and as the hovered tooltip, does not carry the retired restart claim and does state the three measured claims (at once; not loaded at the next start; records kept).
- `no pack's kernel note says the app stays registered until a restart (objectui#12684)`: the retired claim is absent from each of the ten packs, the table names every pack, and no non-en pack serves the en sentence.

These pins read the note's claims, not its whole wording, so a later rewording that keeps the facts does not turn them red.

## Tests and gates (all at `77821a8`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the pins file and `ar-participle-orthography-6610.test.ts`: 2 files, 53 passed.
- Ablation leg A, the ten bundles put back to main's blobs (hash-checked on disk) under the committed tests: **12 failed | 41 passed**. Red: the en and zh rendered pins, and the ten retired-claim rows. Green: every objectui#12610 pin and every objectui#6610 pin. Restored from `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty, every blob equal to `HEAD`.
- Ablation leg B, en only, "at once" dropped (anchor hit once, blob changed, restored blob equal to `HEAD`): **1 failed | 48 passed**. Red: the en rendered pin, on the at-once claim. This shows the positive half can fail on its own.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/ packages/i18n/`: 119 files passed, 1598 passed and 13 skipped.
- `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`: 28 of 28 tasks successful.
- `type-check` of `@object-ui/i18n` and `@object-ui/app-shell`: exit 0. The app-shell test project lists the pins file.
- eslint on the twelve changed source files: 0 errors. One warning: the existing `catch (e: any)` in `doUninstall`, which this PR does not touch.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0 · `pnpm check:new-line-citations` 0 (0 new) · `pnpm check:i18n-keys` 0 · `pnpm check:i18n-drift` 0 (1 en value changed, 9 packs followed) · `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys` 0 (report).
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the diff: NOT GOVERNED.

## Acceptance notes

- **The same stale claim lives in three sibling strings, outside this card's file surface, so they are untouched here.** `marketplace.uninstall.confirm`, `marketplace.uninstall.successInList` and `marketplace.uninstall.successInDetail` still say the app stays loaded until the next restart, in en, zh and ja; the other seven packs never carried that clause. The same run reproduced it in the console. The Uninstall confirm dialog read "The cached manifest will be removed. The app will remain loaded in the running kernel until the next restart." The result line read "Removed com.example.crm. Restart the runtime to fully unload it from the running kernel." Right after that, `GET /api/v1/meta/app` no longer listed `crm_app`. Reported to the seat to file. The comment above `question` in `MarketplaceRowActions` describes those texts and would follow them.
- **objectstack side:** after the DELETE and with no restart, `GET /api/v1/meta/object` (and `GET /api/v1/meta/object/crm_account`) still served the six CRM objects with `_packageId: com.example.crm`. At the same time, `GET /api/v1/data/crm_account` answered 404. A restart cleared the listing. The install-local plugin's docblock says the withdrawal takes "every metadata item it shipped". Reported to the seat; this note makes no claim about the objects' metadata listing.
- The console's `uninstallLocal` reads nothing from the DELETE's 200 answer. The server documents one case where the running kernel refuses the withdrawal (another package extends an object this one owns). In that case the package stays loaded until a restart, and that is reported only as a failed `registry.uninstallPackage` entry in `cleanups`. The console would show plain success, and the note describes the normal path. This was not reproduced, and nothing is filed for it.
- The key's name still says "additive". Renaming it would be a key change across ten packs, the pins and the call site, so it is left as it is.
